newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina signs tanker contracts with local firms.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina signs tanker contracts with local firms.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina on Wednesday signed contracts with 11 local companies for 15 Long Term Time Charter (LTTC) tankers.
Pertamina shipping director Kartiyoso said the tankers, ranging from 1,500 deadweight tonnes (dwt) to 30,000 dwt, will be built by the private companies in 20 to 24 months.
Kartiyoso, who did not say how much the contracts cost, was speaking to reporters after Pertamina signed the charter contracts with the companies in Jakarta.
Another Pertamina official said the tankers are expected to be operational by late 1998.
Pertamina president-director Faisal Abda'oe said Pertamina currently uses 185 tankers but needed more in future.
He said Pertamina owned 68 tankers and chartered the rest.
"Pertamina needs more tankers to distribute oil products throughout the archipelago. Today's signing (of the contracts) will help Pertamina's distribution," he told reporters.
